trigger: the MARKS legend sheet's TRAP row, and the hold-inspect card on a seen trap square
before: A d6 out of you, before you knew it was there.
after: Step on it and a d20 decides: 16–20 dodges it (13–20 for an Acrobat). Fail and it goes off, anything from a d6 of darts to a spike pit's d10×5. Going around is free.
why: The mark is only drawn on a square you can already see, springTrap rolls a d20 dodge first, and the trap table runs from a d6 to a spike pit's d10×5, so neither "a d6" nor "before you knew" was true.

trigger: the MARKS legend sheet's LOCKED BOX row, and the hold-inspect card on a seen box square
before: 1–5 on a d10 opens it. The rest costs you a pick.
after: With lockpicks or the Locks skill, 6–10 on a d10 opens it (more faces with practice or wits); bare hands need 13–20 on a d20. Fail and it stays shut for good.
why: The range was the retired roll-under face count, it left out the bare-handed d20 roll, and a failed lock never costs a pick: openChest stops at chestLocked and the box's square is already cleared.

trigger: the MAKE CAMP sheet's body, opened from the ☰ menu
before: Eight hours asleep in a corridor that has already killed better people than you. One ration buys the sleep and a full spell book. We roll to see what wanders past.
after: Eight hours asleep in a corridor that has already killed better people than you. Supper is {rations}: it buys the sleep, some HP back and a full spell book. We roll to see what wanders past.
why: A night costs the whole party's nightlyEats (two for a Troll, more with Joiners), not always one ration, and a fed night also heals; the sheet now fills the count from the camp gate's own helper.

trigger: the MAKE CAMP sheet's SLEEP button
why: The button promised one ration to a Troll or a party that eats more; it now shows the real nightly count.

trigger: THE STAIR DOWN overlay, before the descent
before: Floor {n} is colder, longer, and considerably less forgiving. Nobody has asked you to do this.
after: Floor {n} is below, and there is no stair back up. It only gets meaner from here. Nobody has asked you to do this.
why: Every floor is the same 21 by 21 maze, so "longer" was not true; the line now states the fact that matters, that the trip is one way.

trigger: the MAKE CAMP sheet's ration count, filled into the body and the SLEEP button
why: The new ration count ("1 ration", "2 rations") the camp sheet fills in from window.__mzNightlyEats.

trigger: the Oracle line after the first Android back press on a live run
before: Press back again to abandon this delve.
after: Press back again to close the game. This delve is saved for later.
why: A second back press exits the app, and the run is already saved and resumes from ENTER, so nothing is abandoned.

trigger: the Settings sheet's On/Off row for the ☰ ABANDON THIS CHARACTER confirm
why: The row only arms the ☰ Abandon row's second tap; SAVE & QUIT never asks and the back button always asks, so "quit" named the wrong control.
